restoration_note: Teaching 77 enumerates the standard Manichaean four great kingdoms of the world (Babylon-Persia, Rome, Aksum, Sileos/Silis), framed correspondentially as the fourfold ordering of natural dominion (Four = ordered fullness in extension). The closing observation that "none is exalted exceedingly above them" points by negation to the King of Honor's judicial dominion above the firmaments and ultimately to the Father of Greatness. The restorations are highly constrained: an enumerative formula 'ⲧⲙⲁⲍ-X ⲧⲉ ⲧⲙⲛⲧⲣ̄ⲡⲟ ⲛ̄...' iterates four times; visible cross-line traces (ⲧⲙ̄/ⲧⲉ, ⲧⲙⲁⲍϣⲁⲙ̄/ⲧ, ...ⲡⲟ ⲛ̄ⲥⲓⲗⲉⲱⲥ, ⲛⲉⲧϣ.../...ⲡ) fix the ordinals and the formula tags; the four toponyms are fixed by the standard Kephalaia list. All editor proposals confirmed; nothing left unrestorable.
